column1: # One row per file the image lane fetches. An artifact is a byte sequence a
# publisher offers; what it is used for is a component of a bundle in
# scripts/image-models.tsv, and how it is served is a row in
# scripts/image-profiles.tsv. Splitting those three claims keeps one file
# reachable from several bundles: the SD 1.5 diffusion checkpoint carries both
# the sd15-base and the sd15-lcm-v1 bundle, and the sd15-lcm-v1 bundle replaces
# the packaged decoder with a separate VAE artifact while reusing the same
# diffusion bytes.
# scripts/download-sdxs-512.sh fetches three files under one destination
# directory rather than one flat file, because init_from_diffusers_file
# resolves the diffusers layout against three fixed relative paths. Each file
# is its own row here -- sdxs-512-diffusion, sdxs-512-vae,
# sdxs-512-text-encoder -- rather than one row naming the diffusion file,
# because a component is what a placement arm moves and scripts/image-models.tsv
# resolves vae_artifact and text_encoder_artifact to their own bytes rather
# than to `packaged`.
# repository and filename are the publisher coordinates. revision, sha256, and
# bytes are the pin, and they move together: all three read `-` while the file
# is unfetched, and the pin lane sets all three from one verified download.
# scripts/image-registry.sh refuses a partial pin, because a digest without the
# revision it was read at names no source and a revision without a digest
# verifies nothing.
# fetch_script names the downloader the pin lane writes. This file validates
# the name shape rather than testing the path, which is where it diverges from
# scripts/models.tsv: that registry's rows serve, so their fetch scripts exist
# and are executable, while an image row states an admitted source before any
# byte has crossed the network. The pin lane turns the name into an executable
# script that pins revision, byte count, and SHA-256 the way every
# scripts/download-*.sh does.
# component_type states what the runtime does with the bytes: `diffusion` is
# the denoising trunk, `vae` the latent decoder, `tae` a Tiny AutoEncoder
# decoder that reaches sd-cli through --taesd rather than through the VAE
# slot, `text_encoder` the prompt encoder, `lora` a weight delta applied over a
# trunk, and `runtime` an executable or library the appliance builds against.
# A bundle resolves each of its components against this column, so a VAE named
# in the diffusion slot is refused rather than loaded, and the first standalone
# campaign proved a `tae` component refused under the full-VAE metadata check
# (evidence/image-appliance/sdxs-512-standalone/README.md): sdxs-512 ships a
# Tiny AutoEncoder in its packaged vae/ slot, and sd-cli reads it correctly
# only through --taesd.
# license is the publisher's own term, recorded because SD-Turbo ships under a
# non-commercial research community licence where SD 1.5 ships OpenRAIL-M, and
# a bundle inherits the most restrictive licence among its components.
